issues.detail: The Greek 'κεκαθικεν' (kekathiken) means 'has ridden/mounted,' but the Vietnamese 'ngồi lên' (sat on) is a less precise rendering of mounting a beast of burden. However, more importantly, the Greek 'λυσαντες αυτον' (lysantes auton) means 'having loosened/untied it.' The Vietnamese 'mở nó ra' (open it) captures the sense of loosening but misses the specific context of untying a bound animal.
